source.title: SGD on Neural Networks Learns Functions of Increasing Complexity
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Dimitris Kalimeris; Tristan Yang; Benjamin L. Edelman; Fred Zhang; B. Barak

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether vanilla SGD retains generalizing simple classifiers while fitting training data, using mutual-information performance correlation rather than the claim versions’ direct train/test error comparisons.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s reported mutual-information results on natural and synthetic classification tasks and its simplified overfitting theorem. Figure-only qualitative train/test behavior is not converted into numbers. Cited results from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests SGD's tendency to learn and retain simpler predictive functions, using performance correlation and a simplified theorem. None of V1–V8 names this relationship. Fitting partially noisy labels while retaining generalization does not establish V1's comparison between fixed random labels and natural labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors present experimental evidence that SGD initially learns predictions explained by linear classifiers and retains simpler predictive information during later fitting. Increasing complexity beyond linear models remains a conjecture supported by shallow-CNN comparisons; the retention theorem applies only to a simplified sparse linear setting.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies SGD dynamics and performance correlation with simpler classifiers rather than the direct interventions and measures in the listed versions; it uses binary classification tasks and a simplified linear theorem.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports less clear phase separation for the 4- and 6-layer conditional CNNs than for the 2-layer CNN and linear model; it attributes this potentially to imperfect simple-model recovery or layer count being an imperfect simplicity measure.

fits_no_version.finding: Early SGD performance is substantially explained by a linear classifier: Table 2 reports performance-correlation ratios of 0.74–0.80, exceeding matched null-model ratios of 0.02–0.52.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested binary tasks, SGD initially learns predictions whose success is largely explained by a linear classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Shallow CNNs explain successive stages of ResNet learning, with ratios of 0.68–0.72 versus null ratios of 0.20–0.40; separation is less clear for the four- and six-layer models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can learn predictive components of increasing complexity, although the apparent phase separation depends on the chosen simpler model.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 gives limiting sample accuracy 1 and population accuracy 1 − p for a sparse linear distribution under specified initialization bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this simplified setting, SGD can interpolate noisy training examples while retaining optimal population accuracy.

record.problems: The authors describe several findings as evidence or conjecture rather than a general theorem; the main experiments are binary classification and use mutual-information correlation as a proxy for performance. The generalization theorem is restricted to a simplified sparse linear model. Some figure descriptions do not provide numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No required numeric table rows were omitted. Figures 4 and 5 include curves and standard-deviation shading, but exact intermediate values are not stated and were not transcribed. Figure 8 reports a qualitative example of continuing training from a bad initialization; no numeric population-accuracy value is given.

untested.parts: No matched training on fixed random labels and natural labels with held-out accuracy comparisons. Partially noisy synthetic labels and the bad-initialization construction do not supply that comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison or intervention on local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No controlled batch-size comparison, epoch-budget comparison, or large-batch recipe adaptation.
No dropout intervention; omitting regularization throughout does not test its effect.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
No influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: T6 is relative to the eight supplied versions. The paper conducts original generalization research, but its own results concern a different relationship. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment trains the same network and recipe on fixed random labels and natural labels and compares their held-out performance.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold or test-error curve by width.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks for image test error.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch generalization-gap experiment.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples and retraining comparison.

rows.subject: CNN with 4 2D-Conv layers and two Dense layers
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional layers, each with 32 filters of size 3 × 3; two Dense layers of 2000 units
rows.operation_detail: Measured the performance correlation of SGD classifier with a linear classifier during training on Binary MNIST.
rows.measure: µY(FT0; L)/I(FT0; Y), linear model; train/test accuracy and mutual-information trajectories shown in figure
rows.uncertainty: standard deviations reported in figures (shaded area); table value has no separate uncertainty
rows.note: Table 2 reports the linear-model ratio; the null-model ratio is listed as the reference. This measures explanation of classifier performance by a linear model, not the direct train/test error gap.
rows.check: The 0.79 versus 0.52 performance-correlation comparison measures explanation by a linear classifier, not any listed version.
